refactor_oracle.why: Both the SET of normalised assert names and the COUNT are pinned, because they are blind to different things - the coordinator's correction to my earlier rule: a set is blind to MULTIPLICITY (a loop over fewer keys leaves names identical while the count drops), a count is blind to SUBSTITUTION (one assert vanishing as another appears).
refactor_oracle.method: PASS lines, strip ' :: …', then normalise runs of FOUR OR MORE digits to N, then sort -u. Compare both directions with comm.
refactor_oracle.a_false_positive_my_own_extraction_produ: First run of this oracle reported one LOST name: 'both dictionary regions are locatable — SETTINGS_I18N at 184726, ru at 200966' against '… at 184746, ru at 200986'. That is ONE assert whose message interpolates measured indices, and dist moved 20 bytes, so the index moved and my extraction read it as a different name - a false substitution manufactured by the instrument. Fixed by normalising digit runs. NOTE THE REFINEMENT: normalising ALL digits would collapse 'No.894', 'No.898' and 'No.880' into 'No.N' and destroy the names' distinctiveness, so only runs of 4+ digits are normalised - indices are 5-6 digits, task numbers are 3. Verified after the refinement: No.894 names 3, No.898 names 39, No.880 names 11, all still distinguishable.
